items.title: Compute the actual signed Gaussian test expectation

source.anchor: Appendix B.2.2: Gaussian density p_O, bounded test h_lambda, H definition Ex56, Ex58/Ex59/Fubini, Ex60 and Eq21; Eq4/Eq26 providers. Conditioned-mixture Ex57/Eq20 remains separate.
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. Actual law-to-density expectation transport and all required L1 conditions are explicit elaborations of the density-based source calculation.

items.statement: Let \(n\ge3\), \(\kappa\ge4\), \(\ell\ge0\), and let \(\mu\) be normalized Haar probability on the full real orthogonal group. For each \(O\), set \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I_n-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), \(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\), \(p_O(x)=\frac{\sqrt{\det A_O}}{(2\pi)^{n/2}}e^{-x^\top A_Ox/2}\), and \(t_\ell(x)=e^{-\ell\|x\|_2^2}\). Then \(t_\ell\in L^1(\gamma_O)\), \(t_\ell p_O\in L^1(dx)\), and \(\int t_\ell\,d\gamma_O=\int t_\ell p_O\,dx\) for every \(O\). The signed expectation is absolutely integrable under \(\mu\), and its average is the displayed formula, with \(U=O_{11}\). The endpoint \(\ell=0\) is included; half-dimension powers use real division. Integrability and density transport are conclusions, with no extra premise. Conditioned target mixtures and the total-variation interpretation remain open.
assumptions: Exactly \(n\ge3\), \(\kappa\ge4\) and \(\ell\ge0\); the endpoint \(\ell=0\) is included.
\(O\) ranges over the full real orthogonal group, with its normalized Borel Haar probability \(\mu\), including both determinant signs.
\(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\) is the canonical Gaussian measure; \(dx\) is Euclidean volume and \(\|x\|_2\) is the true Euclidean norm.

The proof establishes \(t_\ell\in L^1(\gamma_O)\), \(t_\ell p_O\in L^1(dx)\), and \(\int t_\ell\,d\gamma_O=\int t_\ell p_O\,dx\) for every \(O\). It also proves absolute Haar integrability of \(O\mapsto\det(O)\int t_\ell\,d\gamma_O\). These are conclusions, with no extra integrability premise.
Dimension-half powers use real division. Positivity, density measurability and the law-to-density identity are proved internally.
